summary: A steel tower on Camp Creek Bald (built 1928 per NHLR, 1929 per another register) got a rare round cab in the 1960s and now sits locked and crowded by antennas on the Appalachian Trail.

facts.design: Round steel observation cab (installed 1960s, one of only two prototype round cabs built), replacing the original 14x14 ft square cab on a steel tower
facts.status_note: Condition has varied by visit: good and intact in a September 2008 report; peeling paint, broken glass and poor wood condition by a September 2020 report, with the volunteer visitor warning the Forest Service might eventually remove it

access.note: Cab trapdoor and catwalk gate are locked (the gate wrapped in razor wire); tower is not open to climb; no formal signage beyond a video-surveillance warning; communication antennas occupy three sides of the site

visit.trail_note: Short side trail off the Appalachian Trail, about 0.2 mile with roughly 150 ft of climb; the tower itself is locked and not open to climb

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Pisgah National Forest, Appalachian Ranger District (cooperator: Andrew Johnson Amateur Radio Club)

events.note: NHLR gives a 14x14 ft cab on a 21-ft steel tower, built 1928
A separate eastern-US lookout register instead dates the same-size 14x14 ft cab to 1929 on a 20-ft tower; the two sources do not agree and neither explains the other's figure
Original square cab replaced with a round cab, one of only two round-cab prototypes the Forest Service built; exact year within the 1960s not given by either source
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register April 2, 2008, as US 719 / NC 13, nominated by Peter Barr

corrections.proposed: Consider adding "Viking Mountain" as a historical alternate name for the site
corrections.evidence: A local history blog states the peak was known as Viking Mountain during a short-lived 1960s-70s ski resort on the mountain, and that the tower predates and outlasted that name. This is a single, lower-reliability source and is not corroborated elsewhere in this research.

corrections.proposed: Unresolved conflict, no change recommended without a tie-breaking source: NHLR gives 1928 and a 21-ft tower; the Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com) page gives 1929 and a 20-ft tower, for an apparently identical 14x14 ft cab.
corrections.evidence: Both pages are the only cached/found descriptions of the original construction; neither cites a further source for its figure.

sources.title: Camp Creek Bald Lookout
sources.publisher: Fire Lookouts of the Appalachian Trail, willhiteweb.com

sources.title: Once Viking Mountain, Always Camp Creek Bald

notes_for_editor: NHLR is detailed and includes two dated visit reports (2008, 2020), giving good texture on condition change over time. The build year (1928 vs 1929) and tower height (21 ft vs 20 ft) conflict between NHLR and the Forest Lookouts site; left unresolved. The Earl Shaffer 1948 overnight-stay claim and the 'Viking Mountain' alternate name both come from a single blog post and are not corroborated elsewhere; flagged in the story and as a proposed correction rather than treated as settled fact. No NRHP nomination or newspaper coverage was found for this tower.
